A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KLAY work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support comparison, including the later additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original circuit-runtime experiments, neurosymbolic benchmarks and MNIST-addition training timings in Section 6 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds neural-network forward/backward timings in Tables 1 and 3.

M1.justification: Layerization, Merkle-hash deduplication, tensorization and evaluation Algorithms 1-4 are unchanged. Appendix D illustrates the existing approach without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic 3-CNF circuits compiled using SDD and D4, plus Sudoku, Grid, HMLC, Warcraft and MNIST-addition tasks. Appendix D's zero/one-digit example is explanatory, with no new empirical task evaluation.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain PySDD/post-order and JUICE, the D4 Rust post-order baseline, naive PyTorch, and DeepProbLog/Scallop. The added Neural rows measure neural components rather than competing circuit-evaluation methods.

E3.justification: Table 1 changes its stated batch size from 1 to 128 while retaining all circuit timings. Table 3 retains different batch-128 timings, and Appendix B still describes a 1-versus-128 contrast. This changes the reported setting without establishing a rerun. v2 also introduces neural-component forward/backward timing measurements.

E4.justification: Tables 1 and 3 add CPU/GPU neural-component timing analyses, providing context for circuit costs relative to neural computation. The existing circuit-size, sparsity and alternative-compiler analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figures 6 and 8 still average ten timing runs per circuit; Table 2 still reports averages and standard deviations over ten epochs. The new neural rows follow the existing uncertainty-reporting format, without introducing new statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 3 add neural-runtime results; for example, Table 3 reports Warcraft neural CUDA time as 73.20 ± 0.02 ms. Existing numerical entries and plotted results are retained, including Table 1's circuit timings despite its changed batch-size caption.

T1.justification: Theorem 1, its Appendix A proof, and the existing definitions and assumptions are unchanged. Appendix D's elementary probability equations instantiate the already described sum/product semantics rather than add a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The claims about knowledge layers, three supporting algorithms, efficient GPU execution and orders-of-magnitude speedups remain unchanged. The more specific title clarifies the existing arithmetic-circuit focus.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly explains that D4 produces smaller circuits and therefore receives harder formulas than the SDD benchmark. This adds a rationale for the differing benchmark construction; the other interpretations and applicability qualifications remain stable.

D1.justification: A new Reproducibility section supplies a KLAY repository address. Appendix B newly specifies variable counts from 30 to 80 in steps of five, ten instances per count, and clause-to-variable ratios for SDD and D4. These document existing experiments rather than establish changed settings.

R1.justification: The reference lists contain the same works, and Section 5 retains the same positioning relative to JUICE, hardware accelerators and probabilistic-circuit systems.

P1.justification: v2 revises the title, publication header, hardware terminology and Section 2 heading. It adds a Reproducibility section, explanatory material in Appendix B and the worked example in Appendix D, while retaining most prose and the main section order.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 9 and neural rows in Tables 1 and 3, reorders their existing rows and revises their captions. Existing figures are retained with some relocation, including grouping Figures 6 and 7 with Table 1.

improvement.justification: The synthetic-generation details, code-access information and worked example modestly improve reproducibility documentation and accessibility. Neural timings add useful context. These gains are tempered by Table 1's changed batch-size caption, which conflicts with the retained Appendix B distinction and Table 3 results, reducing clarity about experimental conditions. The method, proof and principal results remain stable.
